title: Sign-in and sign-up never return to where the person was going (invite link, deep links)
observed: Signed out on /join?code=NHUA1B -> 'Sign In to Join' -> '/login?from_url=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A4607%2Fjoin%3Fcode%3DNHUA1B'. Path A (log in as newbie): 'OK tapped [5] button "Log in" -> now at /home ... ## NO GROUPS YET'. Path B ('Create one' -> /register, the query string is already gone; new e-mail, any 6 digits): 'OK tapped [2] button "Verify" -> now at /home' with 'NO GROUPS YET'. Deep link signed out: 'OK loaded /round/579ae075098281d89c967fb0 -> redirected to /home' (the landing page, not the login form); localStorage base44_from_url held the round address and was not used.

cause.what: After a password login the page is always set to '/home'; nothing reads the from_url parameter.
Google sign-in is started with the fixed return address '/home'.
The 'Create one' link goes to plain /register, dropping the from_url query.
After the verification code the page is always set to '/home' (same at line 70 for Google).
Sends the signed-out visitor to login through the SDK, which adds ?from_url=<invite link> - the only place the invite is carried.
The existing safe-redirect helper reads a parameter called returnTo (not from_url) and is not called by Login or Register at all.
A signed-out visitor on any group page (/session, /round, /player, /admin) is redirected to /home instead of /login, with no return address.
base44_from_url in localStorage is overwritten with the current address on every page load, so it cannot be relied on as the return address.

notes: One fix covers all three findings: Login and Register must read the return address (validate it with safeReturnTo) and go there after sign-in, and the Login -> Register link must keep it. qa-tester-2 adds the landing-page redirect in Layout.jsx:52.

observed: Transcript .../scratchpad/review/rules-assistant-live.txt: 'Q: מה קורה אם כולם נופלים?' / 'A: "Everyone Falls" — the round is cancelled, everyone's contract points are zeroed, ...'.

cause.what: The system prompt (244-252) says nothing about the language of the answer, and line 248 tells the model to 'use the rulebook's wording', which is English.

notes: Only the prompt needs a line; the rulebook can stay English.

title: The assistant's refusal is 'IDK bro' and a dead end; one answer left out the other progressive tiers
observed: Transcript: 'Q: How do I delete my account?' / 'A: IDK bro 🤷 — that's not in the WhistMate rulebook.'

cause.what: The refusal line is a constant, and the prompt orders the model to reply 'EXACTLY this and nothing else' for anything off-topic, naming accounts explicitly (249-251).
'Keep answers short and plain' - which is how a miss-by-5 question gets only the miss-by-5 tier, although the rulebook has all four (docs/whist-rules.md:216-220).
The chat falls back to the same line when no answer comes.

notes: Intended (docs/whist-rules.md:21 calls it 'the "IDK" refusal'). Tone and a pointer to About / My Account are the lead's decision. The tier omission is one real-model answer and cannot be re-run in the sandbox.

title: New Session ignores the group's default scoring and Advanced setting after a reload or direct open
observed: Family Table (default Progressive): START NEW SESSION -> buttons '["Classic:-","Progressive:SELECTED"]'. Reload -> '["Classic:SELECTED","Progressive:-"]'. Start Session -> '# Whist Night / ... · Open · Classic'.

cause.what: The scoring method and the Advanced switch (22) take their starting value from the group once, on first render; on a reload or direct open the groups are still loading then, so both start as Classic / off and are never updated.
The form always sends its own value, so the server's fallback to the group default (startSession/entry.ts:92-93) never applies.
Groups load asynchronously; Layout.jsx:52 lets the page render while they do.

notes: The rules are frozen for the session and there is no edit or delete for a session, so a wrong method cannot be undone.

observed: Deleted round 2 of 4: list 'Round 4, Round 3, Round 1', button 'START ROUND 4'; the round it created was headed 'BIDDING | Round 5 · step 1 of 2'.

title: Session name, location and date accept anything; a blank date is saved as the day before (shortly after midnight)
observed: At 01:12 local time (23:12 UTC, 18 Nov) on Thursday 19 Nov: cleared the Date field (form default was 2026-11-19), Start Session -> '# Whist Night / Nov 18, 2026 · Open · Classic'; the stored row has session_date '2026-11-18', created_date '2026-11-18T23:12:25.582Z'.

cause.what: When no date arrives the server uses new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10) - the UTC day, which in Israel is still yesterday until 02:00 (03:00 in summer).
Name and location (89) are trimmed but have no length limit, and the date is not checked for a sane range.
The date field can be emptied and the form still submits; the name and location inputs have no maxLength (61, 69).
The title has no wrapping or truncation, so a long unbroken name widens the page.

notes: TIME ZONE: yes, this is the time-zone effect of the server default - the same trap src/lib/format.js:12-14 describes and avoids on the client. SANDBOX CLOCK: not the cause. The sandbox simulates the clock only while it seeds (sandbox/backend.mjs:527-549); a request is stamped with the real clock, and 23:12 UTC on the 18th is the true time. It reproduces only between local midnight and 02:00/03:00, which is when the QA tester and I happened to be working. Fix on both sides: the form should refuse or refill a blank date, and the server should not guess a day from UTC. NEW (not in any report, computed in the page, not tested with a real device setting): date-only values are parsed as UTC midnight by formatDate (src/lib/format.js:25), so west of UTC every session date is shown one day early - new Date('2026-11-19') formatted for America/New_York gives 'Nov 18, 2026'.

title: An archived group still offers every write action; they fail only at the last step
observed: Seen: after Archive the header shows ARCHIVED and Admin still offers every control. Reviewer output: '! http 403 ... startRound — {"error":"This group is archived — it is read-only"}'.

cause.what: Start / Resume Round, 'Edit round' and Close Session are drawn from the session's state alone; the group's archived status is not consulted (nor in NewRound.jsx or RoundView.jsx).
The read-only banner is shown only when there is no open session.
A failed note delete is only logged to the console.
Closing is refused in an archived group, so a session left open at archive time stays open.

notes: Only PlayerProfile.jsx:136 and Home.jsx:92 react to 'archived' today. Archiving with a session open should either be refused or close it.

With the deleted group gone from the list, the first remaining group silently becomes the current one.

title: Tied players are given different ranks - and two tied leaders are both credited with a win
observed: One round in a new session with two players on +35 and two on -5: '#1 | Maya | 1 round · 1 win · +35 avg | +35 | #2 | נועה | 1 round · 1 win · +35 avg | +35 | #3 | אמא | ... | -5 | #4 | סבא משה | ... | -5'.

cause.what: The rank shown is simply the row's position after sorting (line 25); equal totals are not detected.
The ranking used for wins and podiums DOES share ranks on a tie (1, 1, 3, 3), so both leaders get a win (standings.js:33; computePlayerStats/entry.ts:123 does the same).

notes: CHECKED AS ASKED: there are two rankings in the code and they disagree. The list shows #1 and #2 for equal totals while the win counter treats both as first. Decide one rule (shared rank is what the stats already do) and use rankSession's result for the label too.

title: Idea: Save Round does not notice that the bids were changed by someone else
observed: saveRoundResults receives only tricks and reneges (RoundView.jsx:329).

cause.what: The function reads the stored bids at that moment and scores against them; the request does not say which bids the scorer was looking at.

notes: The data exists on both sides: the client holds the bids it displayed and the round's updated_date, either of which could be sent for the server to compare. Realtime is simulated in the sandbox, so the two-screen case could not be judged there.

title: Idea: Create Group has no server-side guard against a duplicate request
observed: The dialog disables its button while submitting (CreateGroupDialog.jsx:71); the function has no check.

cause.what: The only uniqueness the function enforces is the invite code; nothing compares the name or a request id with a group the caller has just created.

notes: No data to key on today (no request id is sent). A finger cannot trigger it, per the tester.
